question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese Cartaz System and Control Points/Ports]
options: Diu — Western entrance to the Gulf of Khambhat
Goa — Central hub on the western coast of India
Malacca — Strait controlling Indo-China and Spice Islands trade
Aden — Strategic port at the Red Sea entrance under permanent Portuguese sovereignty
wrong_fact: Aden was never under permanent Portuguese sovereignty. Albuquerque's attempt to capture Aden in 1513 failed, and the Portuguese were unable to seal this Red Sea entrance permanently.
explanation: To establish sea control, the Portuguese built fortresses at key choke points (Diu, Goa, Malacca, Ormuz) and enforced the Cartaz (permit) system. Diu controlled the Gulf of Khambhat; Goa was the headquarters; Malacca controlled the eastern entry to the Indian Ocean. However, they failed to conquer Aden, leaving the Red Sea route open to Ottoman and Arab merchants.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Choke Points of Indian Ocean Trade and the Controlling European Powers]
options: Strait of Malacca — Dutch control (from 1641 onwards after capturing from Portuguese)
Sunda Strait — English control (established as their primary exclusive base from 1600)
Bab-el-Mandeb / Aden — Ottoman control (contested by Portuguese)
wrong_fact: The Sunda Strait was controlled by the Dutch East India Company (VOC), which established its headquarters at Batavia (Jakarta) near the strait in 1619, shutting out the English.
explanation: The Portuguese controlled Hormuz from 1515 until 1622 (when a joint Anglo-Persian force took it) and Malacca from 1511 until 1641. The Dutch VOC took Malacca in 1641 and dominated the Sunda Strait from Batavia, leaving the English East India Company to focus on India. The Bab-el-Mandeb/Aden area remained under Ottoman control despite Portuguese naval incursions.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Historical Naval Blocks/Confrontations and their Geographic Context]
options: Blockade of Goa (1638–1644) — Dutch VOC fleets sealing the Portuguese capital from the Arabian Sea
Battle of Swally (1612) — English East India Company victory over the Portuguese off the coast of Surat
Battle of Diu (1509) — Joint alliance of Egypt, Gujarat, and Calicut defeated by Francisco de Almeida in the Gulf of Cambay
Capture of Ormuz (1622) — Joint Anglo-Persian force capturing the fortress from the Portuguese on the Malabar Coast
wrong_fact: Ormuz (Hormuz) is located at the entrance to the Persian Gulf, NOT on the Malabar Coast of India.
explanation: The Capture of Ormuz in 1622 was a critical geopolitical shift where the English EIC assisted the Persian Safavid empire to expel the Portuguese from the Persian Gulf, not the Malabar Coast. The Blockade of Goa (Goa coast), Battle of Swally (near Surat/Gulf of Khambhat), and Battle of Diu (off Diu island) are all geographically and historically correctly matched.
